A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMCCD work and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. Textual and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original IMCCD evaluations on POPE, CHAIR and MME, together with ablations, timing measurements and appendix GPT-4o-assisted evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, with selected POPE scores revised in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical CMVED value masking, contrastive decoding and CDAR attention refinement. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same POPE subsets across MS-COCO, A-OKVQA and GQA, MME tasks, and MS-COCO captioning scenarios, including the appendix evaluations.

E2.justification: Standard decoding, VCD and ICD retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. No comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: The reported models, sample sizes, prompts, metrics and hyperparameters are unchanged, including the appendix caption-length settings. No protocol revision is stated to accompany the Table 1 score changes.

E4.justification: The component and distortion ablations, object-co-occurrence analysis, timing analysis, positional-embedding comparisons, hyperparameter studies and qualitative caption examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statistical reporting, including Figure 5's averaging over five object pairs. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises 24 IMCCD values across six model/subset combinations: MS-COCO Random and GQA Random for both models, plus MS-COCO Adversarial and A-OKVQA Random for InstructBLIP. For LLaVA 1.5, MS-COCO Random accuracy/F1 changes from 89.23/88.68 to 88.77/87.59, while GQA Random F1 changes from 88.80 to 88.96. These are localized score revisions; comparator scores and all other results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention equations, masking formulation and positional-refinement formulation are identical. No theoretical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free hallucination mitigation through CMVED and CDAR, including addressing spurious inter-modality correlations.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same limitations concerning attention magnitude as a proxy for causal relevance and dependence on visual-encoder grounding.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, decoding settings and the statement promising future code availability are unchanged. No new reproducibility information accompanies the revised scores.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning against prior decoding approaches and all 45 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv version/date text changes, from v1 dated 3 January 2025 to v2 dated 11 March 2025. The prose, headings and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 updates some boldface and underlining associated with the revised rankings; for example, VCD's LLaVA 1.5 MS-COCO Random recall becomes bold. Figure content, table structures, captions and placement otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision replaces selected Table 1 scores without explaining whether they correct errors or reflect reruns. The method, experimental coverage, explanations and appendices remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the replacements improve reporting accuracy, so a reliable overall quality direction cannot be assigned.
